monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and frequency compared to last month, with only one run completed so far — but that single run achieved the fastest pace and highest aerobic training effect of the month, suggesting strong acute performance.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite just 1 run this month, the runner achieved their fastest pace (512 sec/km = 8:33 min/km) and highest aerobic TE (3.1) of the month — matching the TE of their three longest runs last month, but at notably higher intensity (54% Z3 vs 31% Z3 last month).

goal_tracker.message: You need 54.5 more km across 10 additional sessions over the next 30 days — averaging 5.45 km per session — to match last month’s volume. At your current pace distribution, prioritize 3–4 Zone 2 runs (HR <140 bpm) and 2–3 mixed-zone endurance runs (Z2/Z3) to rebuild volume sustainably.

insights.title: Efficiency dipped slightly despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.46 to 13.2 m/sec per bpm this month — meaning each heartbeat moved slightly less distance, even though pace improved. This suggests increased cardiovascular demand for the same mechanical output, possibly due to reduced recovery or accumulated fatigue.

insights.title: Overreliance on Zone 3 — missing foundational Z1/Z2 stimulus
insights.body: This month’s run spent only 6% in Z1 and 19% in Z2 — well below last month’s 24% Z1 + 29% Z2 — while Z3 jumped to 54% (vs 31% last month). This indicates a shift toward threshold-focused efforts without sufficient easy-run recovery or aerobic base support.

insights.title: Stride length and vertical oscillation improved with pace
insights.body: From 6/21 (10.5 km, 9:25/km) to 7/1 (6.5 km, 8:33/km), stride length increased from 68.77 cm to 75.77 cm (+7.0 cm) and vertical oscillation rose from 7.7 cm to 8.1 cm — consistent with more powerful, efficient turnover at faster paces, not wasted motion.

insights.title: Aerobic TE is high per run, but total load collapsed
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE is stable at 3.1 (same as 6/21, 6/28, and 7/1), yet total monthly TE dropped from ~30 (11 × 2.7) to just 3.1 — indicating excellent quality but critically low quantity, risking detraining of aerobic capacity if sustained.

recommendations.action: Do a 6 km Zone 2 run tomorrow at avg HR ≤138 bpm (based on last month’s Z2 upper bound and your 6/19 recovery run HR of 112 bpm), keeping cadence ≥150 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your Z2 time dropped to just 19% this month — rebuilding Z2 volume will lower avg HR, improve efficiency, and restore aerobic resilience before adding more intensity.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 6/25 run (3.0 km @ 9:34/km, HR 135 bpm, TE 2.4) as a controlled 'form rehearsal' run — focus on maintaining stride length ≥72 cm and vertical oscillation ≤7.6 cm using real-time ground contact time feedback.
recommendations.reason: That run showed optimal balance of pace, HR, and biomechanics (VO2 max 39.0, GCT 322 ms); replicating it reinforces neuromuscular efficiency at sustainable intensity.

recommendations.action: Add a 20-min post-run walk (no watch needed) after every run this week to actively support parasympathetic recovery — especially given elevated Z3 % and rising vertical oscillation.
recommendations.reason: Your recent Z3-dominant pattern and increased VO (7.9→8.1 cm) suggest accumulating neural fatigue; low-intensity movement enhances blood flow and autonomic reset without adding load.
